Synopsis:
New Fed Chair Kevin Warsh delivered a hawkish-leaning speech at Jackson Hole, signaling the Fed "will have work to do" if inflation doesn't return to 2%. He stopped short of explicitly committing to a September rate hike, consistent with his stated policy of abandoning forward guidance. Markets reacted hawkishly — 2Y Treasury yields rose, September hike odds jumped from 35% to 57%. Investor reaction was mixed: encouraged by clearer inflation resolve, but frustrated by lack of clarity on the Fed's reaction function. All eyes now shift to August payrolls and CPI prints as the next key policy catalysts.

Sentiment: 65 (Meaningfully more hawkish than prior — Warsh's speech shifted September hike odds up sharply by ~22pp, 2Y yields hit a one-month high, and the market read the speech as a clear hawkish step-up relative to his prior two press conferences; however, ambiguity on the precise reaction function prevents a more extreme hawkish reading)
